title: Stoke Space raises another billion to rival SpaceX at re-flying rockets
slides: Who will master rapid rocket reuse besides SpaceX?
Stoke Space just secured an additional billion dollars.
It still hasn't reflown an orbital booster successfully.
This cash targets engines, heat shields, and landing legs.
Watch their next launch—success could reshape the market.
thread_text:
1. Who else is betting big?

Stoke Space just landed an extra billion dollars for rocket reuse—without ever flying a booster to orbit successfully.

2. What the cash is for

The money targets engines, heat shields, and landing legs—the hardest parts of rapid reuse that even SpaceX took years to crack.

3. The unproven hurdle

Stoke has yet to re-fly a single orbital booster. Their next launch is the do-or-die proof.

4. Why this launch matters

A successful reflight would directly challenge SpaceX's dominance in reusable rockets, shaking the market's current order.

5. Watch their next move

Bookmark Stoke's launch schedule. If they nail it, will your investment thesis change?

instagram.caption:
A rocket company just raised another billion dollars without ever successfully re-flying an orbital booster. 🚀

Stoke Space is betting big on engines, heat shields, and landing legs—the same components that took SpaceX years to master. Their next launch will prove whether the technology actually works.

If it succeeds, the monopoly on rapid rocket reuse cracks open. That means cheaper satellite launches and faster iteration for anyone building in space.
